ANALOG ALU
4-bit sequential programming guide

Programs run on a programmed silicon wafer or semiconductor. Values are unsigned 4-bit integers from 0 to 15. Arithmetic results wrap modulo 16. Each statement takes 1 ms.

3. EXPRESSIONS

Literals are 0..15. Use let name = expression; to declare a variable, then name = expression; to assign it.

Precedence, high to low:
* / %
+ - ++ --
<< >> <<< >>>
&
^
|

Use parentheses to group expressions. Values wrap to four bits.

4. OPERATORS

+ add; - subtract; * multiply; / integer divide; % remainder.
<< and >> shift left/right. <<< and >>> rotate left/right.
& bitwise AND; | bitwise OR; ^ bitwise XOR.
++ adds and exposes carry; -- subtracts and exposes borrow.

Unary + and - preserve or negate a value. ~ is 4-bit NOT; ! is logical NOT (0 becomes 15, nonzero becomes 0).

5. FUNCTION FORM

Operators can also be written as calls:
+(a, b)  -(a, b)  *(a, b)
/(a, b)  %(a, b)  &(a, b)
|(a, b)  ^(a, b)  <<(a, b)
>>(a, b)  ++(a, b)  --(a, b)

Unary forms: +(a), -(a), !(a), ~(a). Use value.carry or value.borrow to read the extra result bit.

6. MEMORY AND OUTPUT

Read a storage cell with data[index]. Write with data[index] = value;. FF cells contain one bit; CRAM cells contain 0..255 bytes, while ALU expressions remain 4-bit.

Assign a port to drive it: front = expression;. Use show(expression); to print a value. The front, back, left, and right ports are available as 4-bit inputs and outputs.
